claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is a high-entropy alloy.
The substrate addressed by the hypothesis is equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has good room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has high elevated-temperature yield strength.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
A thin, adherent, alumina-forming coating can be deposited on the as-cast alloy by electrospark deposition or pack cementation.
The coating will form a continuous, dense, and slow-growing Al2O3 layer during exposure.
The alumina layer will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion into HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will rapidly oxidize in high-temperature air to form a stable alumina scale.
Preventing oxygen penetration with the alumina scale will prevent pesting.
The coating treatment will leave the bulk microstructure unaffected.
Leaving the bulk microstructure unaffected will preserve the alloy's room- and high-temperature mechanical properties.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr rapidly oxidizes and undergoes pesting in air at 800 °C.
After approximately 5 hours in air at 800 °C, coated material will have significantly better oxidation resistance and minimal scale spallation or degradation relative to untreated material.
The coated alloy will retain 8–16% room-temperature tensile elongation.
The coated alloy will retain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Protection is expected to remain effective for exposure up to 800 °C for about 5 hours in air, provided that the coating remains intact.
Protection and mechanical retention are expected under mechanical loads and strain-rate conditions similar to the baseline studies.
Long-term coating adhesion and stability under cyclic or prolonged thermal exposure remain unverified.
Possible effects of the coating on fatigue and other dynamic mechanical properties remain unverified.
